result.summary: Updates ArgsManager to support GNU-style option parsing where command-line options are recognized even after non-option arguments. Unrecognized options after commands now produce errors rather than being silently collected as positional arguments, and '--' explicitly terminates option processing. Adapts bitcoin-cli and bitcoin-tx to consume pre-parsed arguments rather than re-scanning raw argv.
result.problem: Previously, any argument following a command was treated as a positional parameter. Options such as -rpcwallet placed after an RPC command were silently ignored or absorbed as positional arguments, potentially targeting the wrong wallet or causing confusing parameter errors.

resolved_concerns: Handling of '--' before the command as well as after the command
Distinguishing Windows path slashes from options with path values
Treating lone '-' and negative numbers correctly as positional arguments
Updating bitcoin-tx to consume filtered arguments so trailing options do not trigger unknown command errors

result.card: This PR adds GNU-style command-line option parsing to ArgsManager so options can appear after commands and positional arguments. It resolves a hazard where options such as -rpcwallet were silently ignored or treated as positional arguments when placed after the command, occasionally directing operations to the wrong wallet. bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-tx, and bitcoin-wallet all benefit from consistent option validation and support for '--'. Review is complete and positive, with an ACK and co-authored fixes from w0xlt.
